account:
Today my routine has included office business, an attempted grain inspection, and tea with my neighbour. The mill visit was inconclusive: I could not find the miller or obtain grain quantities or storage records. That is a gap in the inspection, not evidence of a grain shortage or poor conditions. I gave the secretary a written report; she secured it and plans to seek a follow-up tomorrow at ten, subject to checking my appointments and obtaining the miller's confirmation.

The unusual business is an eighteen hundred great hall lighting inspection with the builder, added to my usual appointments. The secretary recorded a signed addendum and has repeatedly confirmed it. The baker says freight confirmed delivery of eighty contracted loaves to the hall, and freight also told him about the lighting appointment. This suggests hall preparations involving bread delivery and lighting, but I have not learned what larger occasion, if any, they serve. My neighbour also knows about the inspection and offered to accompany me. I cannot infer any hidden purpose from their interest.

Workers near the mill repeated a rumour about a bridge or port change associated with the bakery, naming the baker, innkeeper and neighbour as present. I have seen no proposal or supporting evidence. The secretary has reported no council letters or decision matters, so that rumour remains unverified rather than town policy.

I found my neighbour at the cottage near (16, -60, 105). They describe a peaceful day at the docks. Tea has been cordial, but I now need to leave for my sixteen thirty office appointment before the eighteen hundred hall inspection.
